cons.claim: Same-day identical evidence treatment is laborious and must be redone whenever a constraint changes
cons.example: one newly remembered specialist forces the network dimension to be rebuilt across the whole candidate set

failure_modes: letting the candidate set be habit, carrier familiarity or convenience rather than recorded need
comparing plans on evidence gathered at different times or from different plan years
hiding the boundary of the agent's shelf so the client believes the set is the whole market
acceptance_tests: every candidate in the file carries a recorded inclusion reason traceable to the intake or a verification record
the file shows all candidates evaluated from current plan-year sources with the dates recorded, and states any need the agent's shelf cannot cover
revisit_triggers: any verified constraint changes: a provider, a drug, the service area, assistance status or the client's exposure preference
a new plan-year document set publishes for the service area
the agent's available shelf changes through a new or lost appointment

nodes.definition: Present the comparison so the beneficiary can decide, which is a discipline with specific rules rather than a style. The trade-offs are stated in both directions for every candidate, in the client's own vocabulary, tied to their own doctors and drugs rather than to abstractions; the material limits are said out loud rather than left in a document, including networks, referral and prior-authorization friction, what happens away from home, what the plan does not cover, and the plan-year variability of anything presented as a benefit. Extra benefits are described with their real constraints, not as free. Fear is not a tool: the cost of being wrong is described factually and only where it is real, and no urgency beyond the actual window is manufactured. When the client asks the agent to choose, the answer restates their own stated priorities and the mechanism that follows from each, offers a decision aid such as which risk they would rather carry, and stops short of a directive; a client who still cannot decide is offered another session rather than a nudge. The step ends with a comprehension check and a record of what the client chose and why in their words.

included: two-directional trade-off statements per candidate in the client's own vocabulary
spoken disclosure of networks, friction, away-from-home rules, exclusions and plan-year variability
the no-fear-selling and no-manufactured-urgency rules, and the scripted answer to the pick-one request
the closing comprehension check and the recorded client rationale
excluded: making the choice, ranking the candidates, or expressing a personal preference as guidance
the regulatory wording of required disclosures and materials, which the certifications and marketing KB owns
presenting any figure not traceable to a current plan-year source in the file

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: post-enrollment surprises, complaints or carrier monitoring indicate that a material limit is not reliably reaching clients during presentation

pros.claim: Two-directional presentation produces decisions clients can still defend to themselves months later
pros.example: a client who chose lower premium with more friction remembers accepting that trade rather than feeling misled in March

pros.claim: A prepared answer to the pick-one request keeps the boundary intact under real pressure
pros.example: a client insisting the agent decide is offered their own stated priorities and a second session instead of a directive

cons.claim: Balanced presentation lengthens the session and can raise anxiety in clients who wanted reassurance
cons.example: a client hearing every limitation of every candidate becomes overwhelmed and postpones deciding

cons.claim: Refusing to recommend cedes ground to competitors who will happily name one plan
cons.example: a client compares the agent's neutrality unfavourably with a call-centre representative's confidence

failure_modes: letting enthusiasm about one plan's extra benefits function as a recommendation
using the closing window as pressure rather than as information
recording the client's choice in the agent's words instead of the client's, which hides what they actually understood
acceptance_tests: the file records, for each presented candidate, at least one advantage and one limitation stated to the client
the file records the client's own words for what they chose and why, plus the comprehension check outcome
revisit_triggers: a client later reports being surprised by a limit that should have been said out loud
a comprehension check fails or the client cannot restate the trade-off
carrier monitoring or a complaint flags presentation language

nodes.definition: Decide, inside an open election window and for a client who already holds coverage, whether a change is warranted, with staying treated as a first-class documented outcome rather than a failure. The analysis starts from what actually changed: the plan's own plan-year changes in premium, cost sharing, formulary, network, extra benefits or rating; and the client's changes in providers, drugs, residence, travel, assistance status or ability to manage friction. A change is warranted when a specific verified need is no longer met and a candidate meets it materially better on the exposure picture. Against that sit the costs a switch can carry: leaving a supplement may mean underwriting to return, some rights are one-time or trial-limited, the client must re-establish providers and prior authorizations, and any accumulated year-to-date spending position may reset under the new plan's rules. When nothing material changed, the outcome is a recorded stay with the reasoning attached, which is exactly the outcome a compensation-neutral practice must be able to produce often.

included: the change inventory on both sides: the plan's plan-year changes and the client's own changes
the warranted-change test tied to a specific unmet verified need
the switching costs: underwriting exposure, one-time or trial-limited rights, re-establishing providers and authorizations, and year-to-date position resets
the recorded stay outcome with its reasoning
excluded: the ongoing annual-review cadence run as a retention practice, which the renewal and retention KB owns
mid-year service problems that create no election right
any assertion about what a plan will do in future years

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: rules governing trial or one-time rights change, or file review shows switches without a recorded unmet need behind them

pros.claim: A documented stay protects clients from churn that serves the agent's activity rather than their needs
pros.example: a client whose plan changed nothing material keeps their coverage with a written note of why no change was made

pros.claim: Naming the switching costs prevents changes that look cheaper and are not
pros.example: a client considering leaving a supplement learns that returning may require underwriting before they decide

cons.claim: Thorough switch analysis takes as long as a new enrollment while often producing no submission
cons.example: a full comparison during the busiest weeks ends in a documented stay

cons.claim: A stay decision can look like inattention if the reasoning is not visible to the client
cons.example: a client who receives no written note assumes their agent simply did not review their plan

failure_modes: switching on a marginal premium difference while ignoring the exposure and friction picture
moving a client out of a supplement without surfacing the underwriting consequence
treating a documented stay as a lost sale and re-opening it with pressure
acceptance_tests: every switch in the file names the specific verified need that changed and how the new plan meets it better
every stay is recorded with dated reasoning that the client also received
revisit_triggers: plan-year change notices publish for the client's current plan
the client's providers, drugs, residence or assistance status change
a right the client holds is one-time or trial-limited and its clock is running

nodes.definition: Submit the enrollment so that everything on it is true and provable. The application must carry the client's identifiers exactly as the administering agency holds them, the effective date the chosen window actually produces, and an election-period basis that matches the verified trigger recorded earlier rather than whichever code processes most easily. The client personally answers every question that is theirs to answer, including any health questions on an underwritten supplement application, and personally signs or provides the electronic or recorded consent the carrier's process requires; the agent never signs for a client, never completes an application while the client is absent, and never smooths an answer to help it through. Where a client is assisted by a representative, the authority for that assistance is documented as the carrier and the rules require. After submission the agent records the confirmation identifier, the submission channel and the date, and tells the client plainly what happens next and by when, because an unconfirmed submission is not an enrollment.

included: identifier accuracy, effective-date correctness and an election basis matching the verified trigger
personal attestation and signature or recorded consent by the client, and documented authority when a representative assists
confirmation identifier, channel and date recorded at submission, and a plain statement of what happens next
excluded: the carrier's processing, underwriting and acceptance decisions
the agency-wide submission platform and its administration
correcting an agency record of the client's identifiers, which the client pursues with the agency

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: carriers or official guidance change submission, consent or effective-date requirements, or rejected submissions reveal a recurring accuracy failure

pros.claim: An election basis that matches verified evidence survives any later review of why the change was permitted
pros.example: a mid-year enrollment questioned months later is explained by the dated event evidence already in the file

pros.claim: Personal attestation protects the client and the agent from an application neither can defend
pros.example: a client answering their own supplement health questions prevents a later dispute about what was disclosed

cons.claim: Insisting on personal completion is slower and can frustrate families used to handling everything
cons.example: an adult child who prepared all the paperwork is told their parent must answer and sign the application themselves

cons.claim: Identifier and effective-date precision depends on records the agent cannot verify directly
cons.example: a mismatch between the client's card and their agency record is only discovered when the submission is rejected

failure_modes: choosing an election code because it processes cleanly rather than because it matches the verified event
completing or signing any part of the application on the client's behalf
treating submission as completion and never capturing the confirmation identifier
acceptance_tests: every submitted application in the file has a recorded election basis matching dated evidence and a confirmation identifier with its date and channel
the file evidences personal client attestation and signature or recorded consent, and documented authority for any representative involved
revisit_triggers: a submission is rejected, pended or questioned on its election basis or identifiers
the carrier changes its signature, consent or submission requirements
official guidance changes effective-date rules for a period class

nodes.definition: Assemble, per enrollment, the artifact set that lets someone reconstruct the whole decision without the agent present: the dated precondition entry; the contact-permission and scope records that permitted the conversation; the intake in the client's words; the verified drug profile with the tool outputs, sources and dates; the provider verification log with sources, dates and who was spoken to; the assistance screening outcome and referral; the comparison worksheet with each candidate's inclusion reason and evidence dates; a note of what was disclosed and presented, including limits stated out loud; the comprehension check and the client's own words about their choice; the election basis with its event evidence; the application confirmation identifier; and copies of anything given to the client. The file is assembled at the time, not reconstructed later, and is stored under the retention obligations that apply, whose current terms and duration are verified with the carriers and the applicable rules rather than assumed. Its test is simple: a reviewer reading it should be able to see why this client ended up with this coverage and that nobody decided it for them.

included: the per-enrollment artifact list and the rule that it is assembled contemporaneously
the reconstructability test a reviewer applies to the file
verifying the applicable retention obligation with carriers and current rules rather than assuming a duration
excluded: the agency-wide documentation, retention and audit programme and its systems, which the certifications and marketing KB owns
call recording infrastructure and its legal requirements
complaint handling and regulator correspondence procedure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: retention or documentation obligations change, or a review shows files that cannot reconstruct the decision they record

pros.claim: A contemporaneous file answers questions years later that memory cannot
pros.example: an inquiry about an enrollment from a previous plan year is answered from the dated verification log and comparison worksheet

pros.claim: The reconstructability test is a practical quality check on the whole process, not just on paperwork
pros.example: a file that cannot show why a candidate was included exposes a comparison that was never need-driven

cons.claim: Assembling the file consumes time in the busiest weeks and pays nothing immediately
cons.example: an extra block after each appointment for filing competes directly with another booking

cons.claim: Retaining detailed client information creates a data-protection burden that must itself be managed
cons.example: drug lists and provider records require secure storage and disciplined access control

failure_modes: reconstructing the file after the fact from memory, which produces a tidy record of work that was not actually done
keeping the application while losing the verification evidence that justified it
assuming a retention period instead of verifying the obligation with the carrier and current rules
acceptance_tests: a reviewer with only the file can state why each candidate was compared and why the client chose what they chose

each enrollment file contains the precondition entry, intake, drug and provider verification evidence, comparison worksheet, disclosure and comprehension notes, election basis evidence and confirmation identifier
revisit_triggers: a carrier or regulator changes what must be retained or for how long
a file review finds a missing artifact class
the practice changes how enrollments are captured or stored

nodes.definition: Close the loop after submission, because an application is a request and coverage is a state. The agent tracks the submission to an outcome, confirms the effective date the client will actually have, and follows up on anything pended, rejected or altered in processing, including a supplement application that comes back underwritten differently from what was applied for, which must be re-presented to the client rather than accepted on their behalf. Before the coverage starts the client is prepared for the first weeks: what their cards will be and when, what to do if a card has not arrived, how the first pharmacy fill should go and what to do if the counter price is not what the estimate suggested, which providers to confirm at the first visit, and how to reach the plan and the agent. Any prior-authorization or continuity-of-care step the new plan requires is identified so it is started rather than discovered at a cancelled appointment. The step ends by handing the client into the ongoing service relationship, whose cadence, review practice and retention purpose belong to the renewal and service knowledge base.

included: tracking the submission to an outcome and confirming the actual effective date
handling pended, rejected or differently-issued outcomes by returning them to the client
first-weeks preparation: cards, first fill, first visit, prior-authorization and continuity steps, and who to contact
the handoff into the ongoing service relationship
excluded: the ongoing service model, mid-year problem resolution and the annual review cadence, which the renewal and retention KB owns
claims, appeals and billing disputes once coverage is in force
any promise about how a specific claim or authorization will be decided

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: carrier processing behaviour or member onboarding changes, or early-weeks problems recur in a pattern the current handoff does not prevent

pros.claim: Tracking to an outcome catches the enrollments that silently failed to take effect
pros.example: a pended application discovered before the plan year starts still has window left to fix

pros.claim: First-weeks preparation converts the most common early failures into expected events with a script
pros.example: a client whose first pharmacy price differs from the estimate knows to call before abandoning the prescription

cons.claim: Follow-through lands immediately after the busiest season, when capacity is already spent
cons.example: confirmation calls compete with the last wave of appointments in the final days of the window

cons.claim: Proactive contact after enrollment is itself governed by contact rules and cannot be improvised
cons.example: a helpful check-in must respect the permission and communication rules that apply to the relationship

failure_modes: treating a confirmation identifier as proof the coverage exists
accepting a supplement offer issued on different terms without returning it to the client to decide
leaving the client without a first-fill or first-visit script so ordinary friction becomes a crisis
acceptance_tests: every submission in the file has a recorded outcome and a confirmed effective date, or an open follow-up with a next action and date
the client received a written first-weeks summary naming cards, first fill, first visit, any authorization step and who to contact
revisit_triggers: a submission is pended, rejected or issued on different terms
the client reports a missing card, a first-fill surprise or a provider refusing the plan
the carrier changes its processing timelines or its member onboarding materials

edges.why_related: the protection protocol operationalizes the boundary: once the decision is the client's, the agent's obligation becomes making sure they can actually make it
the neutrality rule is what makes the educational boundary credible rather than decorative
the period map is only worked once the contact itself is permitted and the plan year's certifications are verified
the eligibility-onset case is one class on the map, worked in detail because its consequences are long-lived
employer coordination is the branch of the onset case where other coverage may permit a delay
the annual window on the map is what turns the calendar into the practice's season plan
the special classes are the event-triggered branch of the same period system
intake is conducted at the pace and with the support the protection protocol requires, including who is present
the medication profile is the deep verification of one intake field
network verification is driven entirely by the providers and travel pattern the intake captured
a supplement is defined by the base program's cost sharing that it pays, so the base must be understood first
the advantage route is an alternative delivery of the same base entitlement and is only intelligible against it
the verified drug profile is the input that produces each candidate's drug picture
the dated verification log is what allows a network claim to appear in the comparison at all
the comparison can only weigh network, friction and annual-limit dimensions once the route's mechanics are held clearly
tier, access-rule and pharmacy-network mechanics are what make a per-plan drug output readable rather than a number
presentation delivers the comparison; without the exposure picture there is nothing neutral to present
an application follows a decision the client made and understood, evidenced by the comprehension check
the submission and its election basis are the last artifacts the case file closes around
the confirmation step records its outcome into the same file and completes it
neutrality constrains what may enter the candidate set and the recorded rationale: needs may, compensation may not
edges.risk_of_conflict: a shortlist shaped by what pays better becomes indefensible the moment anyone reads the file

edges.why_related: the protection protocol constrains presentation pace, session length, materials and the stop condition
no application may be submitted for a carrier or plan year the precondition entry does not cover
the election basis recorded on the application is constrained to a trigger class with dated evidence in the file
assistance status changes the cost model and sometimes the plan set, so an unresolved status constrains the comparison to a provisional label
the two routes trade predictable premium and provider freedom against lower recurring cost, bundled extras and network plus utilization-management friction
edges.resolution_rule: neither route dominates; the choice is decided by the client's verified needs (named providers, drug list, travel pattern, friction tolerance, tolerance for variable point-of-care cost and for future underwriting exposure) and the deciding need is recorded in the file, with the beneficiary making the election

edges.why_related: season throughput pressures the pacing, second sessions and comprehension checks that protect the client
edges.resolution_rule: the protection protocol wins: reduce bookings, use reserved second-session capacity, or refer the client onward, and never compress or skip the comprehension check to fit a slot

edges.why_related: a switch can produce enrollment compensation while a stay produces none, which is exactly the pressure neutrality exists to remove
edges.resolution_rule: no switch is submitted without a recorded verified need that the current plan no longer meets; compensation never appears in the analysis or the rationale, and a documented stay is treated as a successful outcome

edges.why_related: the plan that best covers the verified drug list is frequently not the plan that keeps the client's treating providers in network
edges.resolution_rule: size both exposures from verified evidence, present them side by side in the client's own terms with what each would mean in practice, and let the beneficiary choose which continuity matters more; record the trade-off and the client's stated reason rather than breaking the tie for them

edges.why_related: clients often want a direct recommendation, which a neutral presentation cannot give without crossing the educational boundary
edges.resolution_rule: the boundary holds: answer by restating the client's own priorities and the mechanism that follows from each, offer a decision aid framed as which risk they would rather carry, and offer another session rather than a directive; never record a plan choice the client did not make

edges.why_related: a wrong call about whether other coverage permits a delay is what causes a missed onset window, a coverage gap and lasting penalty-class exposure
because the route's terms are set one plan year at a time, its annual changes are what generate the switch-or-stay question every year
an imprecise medication profile is the usual cause of the first-fill surprise the confirmation step has to catch and explain
establishing that a right to elect exists comes before spending an appointment building a comparison the client cannot act on
submission is followed by tracking to an outcome and confirming the effective date before the client is handed off
what surprises clients in their first weeks tells the practice which intake question was missing or too shallow
each season's rule changes, rejected elections and effective-date surprises are what refresh the period map for the next plan year

both are separately purchased layers on the base program whose benefit content is defined outside the carrier, so both are shopped on carrier price, stability and service rather than on benefit richness

conflict_axes.name: premium_certainty_vs_pay_as_you_use_exposure
conflict_axes.description: A steady predictable premium that converts most point-of-care cost into a known number, versus a lower recurring cost with variable cost sharing bounded by the plan's own annual limit and paid mostly by people who use care.
poles: pay a steady premium for predictability
pay less monthly and more at the point of care
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: decide from the client's verified use pattern, their ability to absorb a bad year, and their stated preference, not from which one the agent finds easier to explain; present both directions and let the beneficiary choose

conflict_axes.name: drug_fit_vs_provider_continuity
conflict_axes.description: The plan that covers the client's verified medication list most cheaply is frequently not the plan that keeps their treating doctors and hospital in network.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: quantify both exposures from verified evidence, present what each would mean in the client's own year, and let them choose which continuity matters more; record the trade-off in their words

conflict_axes.name: season_throughput_vs_conversation_quality
conflict_axes.description: The annual window concentrates demand into weeks while an honest comparison for a complex client takes far longer than a convenient appointment slot.
poles: serve everyone who asks in the window
protect the quality floor of each conversation
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: size bookings to the real length of the work, front-load materially changed plans, hold reserve capacity for second sessions, and refer onward once capacity is honestly exhausted

conflict_axes.name: requested_recommendation_vs_education_boundary
conflict_axes.description: Clients frequently ask the agent to choose for them, which is the moment the educational boundary is either kept or quietly abandoned.
poles: give the client the direct answer they asked for
hold the boundary and keep the decision with the beneficiary
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: answer with the client's own priorities and the mechanism each implies, offer a which-risk-would-you-rather-carry frame, and offer another session rather than a directive

conflict_axes.name: compensation_incentive_vs_need_driven_selection
conflict_axes.description: Compensation differs by product class and by whether an enrollment counts as new, which creates a standing pull on which candidates get built and how a switch question is framed.
poles: follow the economics of the practice
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: needs decide the candidate set and the rationale; compensation is disclosed as a mechanism when asked and audited for concentration afterward, never used as an input

conflict_axes.name: deadline_pressure_vs_verification_completeness
conflict_axes.description: A closing window pushes toward electing on unverified provider and drug claims, while every unverified claim is a January failure waiting to happen.
poles: verify everything before it is presented
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: verify what is decision-critical first; if verification cannot be completed, say plainly which claim is unverified, do not let it carry the decision, and use the remaining window or the next valid one

conflict_axes.name: switch_now_vs_future_optionality
conflict_axes.description: A change that looks better for the coming year can forfeit rights that are hard or impossible to recover, most sharply where returning to a supplement would require underwriting.
poles: preserve the ability to come back
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: state the optionality cost explicitly before the decision and default to staying unless a verified need is unmet; the informed beneficiary still decides

conflict_axes.name: presentation_simplicity_vs_disclosure_completeness
conflict_axes.description: A long technical presentation exhausts an older client's attention while an abbreviated one leaves out limits that matter, and both failure modes end in a client who did not really understand.
poles: simplify to what the client can hold
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: say every material limit out loud in the client's own terms and move the rest into a written keepable summary; use a second session rather than compressing the material limits

conflict_axes.name: caregiver_involvement_vs_beneficiary_autonomy
conflict_axes.description: Family and caregivers make the logistics work and often understand the material faster, which is exactly how they end up making a decision that is not theirs to make.
poles: work through the helpful family member
keep the beneficiary as the decision-maker
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: welcome support, address the beneficiary directly, require their own restatement and their own attestation, and stop if the decision is being driven by someone who benefits from it

edge_cases.description: The plan directory lists the client's specialist as participating, but the specialist's office says they will not accept that plan next year
edge_cases.trigger: directory and provider office disagree during verification
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the office answer as controlling for the decision, record both sources with dates and the person spoken to, tell the client the discrepancy exists, and do not let a directory-only claim carry a decision-critical provider

edge_cases.description: A client's drug appears on the formulary at a favourable tier but is subject to prior authorization or step therapy, so access in January is not what the comparison implied
edge_cases.trigger: formulary listing read as access without checking utilization-management flags
edge_cases.mitigation: record the access flags next to every drug in the comparison, explain what the flag will require at the pharmacy or prescriber, and name the exception and appeal path before the client elects

edge_cases.description: A client moves mid-year to a different service area and their network-based plan no longer works where they live
edge_cases.trigger: permanent change of residence outside the plan's service area
edge_cases.mitigation: verify the move class and its evidence, check the window and effective-date rules for that class in current sources, and rebuild the comparison for the new area rather than transplanting the old shortlist

edge_cases.description: A client believes continuation or retiree coverage counts as qualifying coverage for delaying an election, and nobody has confirmed it
edge_cases.trigger: a coverage class is assumed rather than confirmed during the onset case
edge_cases.mitigation: put the question in writing to the plan administrator and the official program source, record the answer, and build the timeline only on the answer that comes back

edge_cases.description: An adult child answers for the beneficiary throughout the appointment and pushes a specific plan they have already chosen
edge_cases.trigger: a third party assumes the decision-making role
edge_cases.mitigation: redirect every question to the beneficiary, require their own restatement of the trade-off, note the dynamic in the file, and stop rather than submit if the beneficiary cannot express their own choice

edge_cases.description: Partway through a long presentation the client's answers become inconsistent and they cannot restate what the plan does
edge_cases.trigger: a comprehension check fails or fatigue and confusion appear
edge_cases.mitigation: end the session without a submission, leave a plain-language written summary, offer a second session with a trusted person or an independent interpreter, and record the stop and the reason

edge_cases.description: A client insists on changing plans mid-year and no qualifying trigger exists, and asks the agent to find some code that works
edge_cases.trigger: pressure to record an election basis that is not true
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse, explain which window is next and what would create a right before then, record the refusal and the explanation, and offer to prepare the comparison in advance of that window

edge_cases.description: A client considering leaving a supplement is outside any guaranteed-issue circumstance, so returning later could require underwriting they might not pass
edge_cases.trigger: a switch away from a supplement outside a guaranteed-issue class
edge_cases.mitigation: state the one-way risk in plain language before the decision, verify the state's own rules on issuance and any local exception, record that the risk was disclosed, and treat staying as the default absent an unmet verified need

edge_cases.description: A carrier withdraws a plan from the service area and affected clients must move under time pressure with the season already underway
edge_cases.trigger: a plan or contract action by the carrier
edge_cases.mitigation: verify the right the action creates and its window, batch the affected clients into prepared sessions with drug and provider verification done in advance, and keep the comprehension check intact despite the volume

edge_cases.description: A client screens as likely to qualify for an assistance program but the determination is still pending as the window closes
edge_cases.trigger: assistance status unresolved while an election must be made
edge_cases.mitigation: label the comparison provisional, show how the picture would change under each status, record the decision made under uncertainty and the follow-up date, and revisit when the agency answers including any election right the change itself may create

edge_cases.description: A family asks the agent to complete and sign the application because the beneficiary is unwell or unavailable that day
edge_cases.trigger: a request to submit without the beneficiary's own attestation
edge_cases.mitigation: decline, reschedule so the beneficiary can attest and sign personally, or document the representative authority the carrier and rules require, and record what was declined and why

workflow.action: Open the contact by stating the boundary, the limited-carrier disclosure and the pacing plan
workflow.description: Say what the agent will and will not do, that the agent represents a limited set of carriers, and that the decision belongs to the beneficiary; set session length and who else should be present
workflow.artifact: opening record with the disclosure and pacing plan noted
workflow.gate: the boundary, the limited-carrier disclosure and the client's ownership of the decision are recorded before any plan is named

workflow.action: Verify the preconditions for this conversation and this plan year
workflow.description: Confirm license state, plan-year and carrier certification, appointments, contact permission and recorded scope for the product types about to be discussed
workflow.artifact: dated precondition entry listing each verified item
workflow.gate: every item is verified and dated for the current plan year, or the conversation is narrowed or rescheduled accordingly

workflow.action: Determine which election right exists and what it permits
workflow.description: Name the period class, verify its current-year window and effective-date rule from official sources, and confirm what kind of change it allows; for a client aging in, open the onset timeline and the employer-coordination questions
workflow.artifact: election-right determination note with the class, the trigger and the source consulted
workflow.gate: the file names a period class with a verified trigger and a current-year source, or records that no right currently exists and when the next one arrives

workflow.action: Run the needs intake and screen for assistance status
workflow.description: Capture providers, medications and pharmacy, travel and residence, known upcoming care, cost-exposure preference, friction tolerance, extra-benefit priorities and support people in the client's own words, and run the assistance screen with a referral where indicated
workflow.artifact: written intake record with the assistance screen outcome
workflow.gate: every intake field is captured or explicitly marked declined, and the assistance outcome is recorded as confirmed, pending, unknown or declined

workflow.action: Build and confirm the medication profile
workflow.description: Record each drug with name, strength, quantity and frequency confirmed from a label or pharmacy record, capture the pharmacies used, and flag specialty, clinically administered and intermittent drugs
workflow.artifact: verified medication profile with confirmation sources
workflow.gate: no drug remains in the profile without strength, quantity, frequency and a confirmation source

workflow.action: Verify provider participation from two sources
workflow.description: Check each named provider in the specific plan's current directory and confirm with the provider's office, and establish the referral, out-of-network, emergency and away-from-home rules for each plan class considered
workflow.artifact: dated provider verification log naming plan, source and person spoken to
workflow.gate: every decision-critical provider has both a directory check and an office confirmation with dates recorded

workflow.action: Build the need-driven candidate set and the exposure picture
workflow.description: Admit candidates only for recorded needs, run every candidate through the same current plan-year evidence on the same day, and express the result as premium, expected and worst realistic use, drugs, providers, travel, friction and exclusions
workflow.artifact: comparison worksheet with inclusion reasons, evidence sources and dates
workflow.gate: each candidate carries a recorded inclusion reason traceable to the intake or verification record, and any need the agent's shelf cannot cover is stated

workflow.action: Run the switch-or-stay analysis for a client who already has coverage
workflow.description: Inventory the plan's plan-year changes and the client's own changes, test whether a verified need is now unmet, and price the switching costs including underwriting exposure and one-time or trial-limited rights
workflow.artifact: change rationale or a recorded stay decision, given to the client in writing
workflow.gate: a switch names the specific unmet verified need and how the candidate meets it better, or the file records a stay with dated reasoning

workflow.action: Present the trade-offs and let the beneficiary decide
workflow.description: State advantages and limitations for each candidate in the client's own vocabulary, say the material limits out loud including friction and plan-year variability, avoid fear and manufactured urgency, and close with a comprehension check
workflow.artifact: presentation record with the comprehension check and the client's own words for their choice
workflow.gate: each presented candidate has at least one advantage and one limitation recorded, and the client restated the trade-off in their own words

workflow.action: Submit the application on the verified election basis
workflow.description: Enter identifiers exactly, set the effective date the window produces, record the election basis matching the dated evidence, have the client personally answer and sign or give recorded consent, and capture the confirmation identifier and channel
workflow.artifact: submitted application with election-basis record and confirmation identifier
workflow.gate: the election basis matches dated evidence in the file, the client attested personally, and a confirmation identifier with its date and channel is recorded

workflow.action: Confirm the enrollment took effect, complete the case file and hand off
workflow.description: Track the submission to an outcome, confirm the effective date, return any pended, rejected or differently-issued outcome to the client, prepare them for cards, first fill, first visit and any authorization step, and close the case file
workflow.artifact: completed case file with the confirmed outcome and a written first-weeks summary given to the client
workflow.gate: every submission has a recorded outcome or an open follow-up with a next action and date, and the case file passes the reconstructability test

priority_rationale: The frame nodes come first because in this line the right to have the conversation, the boundary of what the agent may say, the protection owed to a protected population and the exclusion of compensation from the reasoning all govern everything downstream; the calendar nodes follow because no comparison is actionable until a verified election right exists and its window and effective-date rules are known; discovery precedes coverage mechanics in practice because the client's own providers, drugs, assistance status and exposure preference decide which mechanics matter; route mechanics are held as structural knowledge so the comparison can be read rather than recited; the comparison, its neutral presentation and the switch-or-stay test sit at the centre because they are where fit is actually decided by the beneficiary; and submission, the case file and the confirmation close the sequence because they convert a decision into coverage that provably took effect and into a record that can be reconstructed later.

dominance_rules.rule: Compliance with the applicable marketing, contact and enrollment rules dominates every growth, throughput or conversion objective
dominance_rules.rationale: this is the most heavily regulated line in the practice; a single rule breach can end the ability to sell at all, which no volume of enrollments compensates for
dominance_rules.trigger: any choice where doing more business conflicts with a rule, a required disclosure or a precondition
dominance_rules.action: take the compliant path, record the decision and the business cost, and escalate to the carrier's compliance contact when the rule is unclear rather than interpreting it favourably

dominance_rules.rule: A verified election right dominates client urgency and agent convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: an election recorded on a basis that is not true is a serious integrity failure, and no client benefit justifies it
dominance_rules.trigger: a client wants a change now and no verified trigger exists, or the cleanest code does not match the actual event
dominance_rules.action: refuse the submission, tell the client which window is next and what would create a right, and record the refusal with its explanation

dominance_rules.rule: Beneficiary autonomy dominates every third party in the room
dominance_rules.rationale: the coverage, the consequences and the decision belong to the beneficiary, and this population is precisely where that is most easily eroded
dominance_rules.trigger: a family member, caregiver or other interested party answers for the client or drives the choice
dominance_rules.action: redirect to the beneficiary, require their own restatement and their own attestation, and stop the process if the decision is not theirs

dominance_rules.rule: Need-driven fit dominates compensation differences without exception
dominance_rules.rationale: compensation is set by regulated schedules for the agent's benefit, not the client's, and letting it shape a shortlist is steering
dominance_rules.trigger: candidates differ in what they pay the agent, or a stay decision would forgo compensation
dominance_rules.action: build and order the set from recorded needs only, keep compensation out of the file's rationale, and let the periodic concentration audit test the result

dominance_rules.rule: Dated primary-source verification dominates memory, last year's file and verbal assurances
dominance_rules.rationale: windows, formularies, networks, extra benefits and cost structures all change by plan year, so anything recalled is likely to be stale
dominance_rules.trigger: any client-facing statement about a window, a drug, a network, a benefit or a cost
dominance_rules.action: verify against the current plan-year official or carrier source, record the source and date, and correct anything already said that the check contradicts

dominance_rules.rationale: an enrollment the client cannot explain back is a failure regardless of how good the fit looks on paper
dominance_rules.trigger: the client cannot restate the coverage mechanism, the main trade-off or what they will pay at the point of care
dominance_rules.action: stop without submitting, leave a written summary, and re-book with a trusted person or an independent interpreter

dominance_rules.rule: Protection of a vulnerable client dominates season capacity
dominance_rules.rationale: the season is a business constraint while the protection protocol addresses irreversible harm to a protected population
dominance_rules.trigger: the booking plan cannot accommodate the pacing, second session or support person a client needs
dominance_rules.action: use reserved capacity, extend into a later valid window, or refer the client onward, and never compress the safeguards to fit a slot

dominance_rules.rule: Preserving the client's future optionality dominates a marginal current-year gain
dominance_rules.rationale: some changes are effectively one-way, most visibly where returning to a supplement would require underwriting the client may not pass
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposed switch would forfeit a guaranteed-issue circumstance or a one-time right for a small improvement
dominance_rules.action: state the optionality cost plainly before the decision, default to staying absent an unmet verified need, and record that the risk was disclosed and what the client chose

dominance_rules.rule: The client's own attestation dominates convenience for everyone involved
dominance_rules.rationale: an application answered or signed by anyone else is indefensible and exposes both the client and the agent
dominance_rules.trigger: a family member or the client asks the agent to complete or sign the application, or to submit while the client is absent
dominance_rules.action: decline and reschedule, or document the representative authority the carrier and the rules require before proceeding

anti_rework_rules.rule: Establish which election right exists before building any comparison
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a full comparison built for a client who has no right to act on it until a later window, which must be rebuilt from fresh plan-year data when the window opens

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify plan-year certification and carrier appointment before naming any plan
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an application that cannot be submitted and a compliance incident that also forces the client conversation to be repeated

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the verified drug profile before shortlisting any drug coverage
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-running the entire comparison when a missed specialty drug or a wrong strength changes which plan is cheapest

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm decision-critical providers with their offices before presentation, not after election
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a January disenrollment scramble for a client whose specialist never accepted the plan, at a point when no election right may exist

anti_rework_rules.rule: Screen assistance status before modelling any costs
anti_rework_rules.prevents: presenting a cost picture built on the wrong cost-sharing basis and having to rebuild both the model and the client's expectations

anti_rework_rules.rule: Ask about travel, a second residence and seasonal living during intake
anti_rework_rules.prevents: choosing a service-area-bound plan for someone who spends months elsewhere and discovering it when they seek care away from home

anti_rework_rules.rule: Establish whether existing coverage is a supplement before discussing any change
anti_rework_rules.prevents: proposing a switch that quietly exposes a client to underwriting they cannot reverse, and the remediation that follows

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record the source and date on every claim as it enters the comparison
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rebuilding evidence from memory at audit, complaint or renewal time, when the plan-year sources have already changed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Ask who else will be part of the decision before the presentation is prepared
anti_rework_rules.prevents: repeating the entire presentation for a family member who was not there and who arrives with a different plan already chosen

iteration_protocol.trigger: plan-year documents, change notices or official guidance publish for the coming year
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify the period map, the route mechanics, formularies and networks, and refresh every reusable template before the season opens

iteration_protocol.trigger: a client reports a first-fill surprise, a denial or a pharmacy price that does not match the estimate
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the medication profile and the plan's current formulary and access rules, explain the exception path, and correct the intake or profiling step that produced the gap

iteration_protocol.trigger: a provider leaves a network, a directory error is found, or a client is told their doctor does not accept the plan
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify participation from both sources, inform the client with the dated evidence, and check whether any election right exists to respond

iteration_protocol.trigger: a comprehension check fails or third-party steering appears in an appointment
iteration_protocol.action: stop without submitting, record the reason, and re-book with a trusted person or an independent interpreter before any presentation resumes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a submission is pended, rejected, questioned on its election basis or issued on different terms
iteration_protocol.action: re-open the election-right determination and the case file, return any altered offer to the client to decide, and correct the submission practice that produced it

iteration_protocol.trigger: a concentration review shows one carrier or product class dominating the book beyond what client needs explain
iteration_protocol.action: audit a sample of comparison worksheets for inclusion reasons, identify where the candidate set narrowed, and correct the selection habit

iteration_protocol.trigger: a client's circumstances change: a move, a coverage loss, an employment change or a new assistance determination
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the period map for a possible right, re-screen assistance status, and rebuild only the affected dimensions of the comparison

iteration_protocol.trigger: the post-season retrospective shows appointments overrunning, comprehension checks skipped or confirmations left open
iteration_protocol.action: resize appointment lengths and reserve capacity, move more verification into pre-season preparation, and close the outstanding confirmations before the next cycle
